title: Bacterial RNA polymerase exemplifies a general physical mechanism for accelerating protein-DNA association
authors: Francis Rivera; Alex Turek; Wencheng Ji; Matt Copeland; Larry Friedman; Fiona Stewart; Johnson Chung; Ariel Amir; Jane Kondev; Jeff Gelles
one_liner_zh: 该文通过单分子实验、动力学模型和布朗动力学模拟，揭示细菌RNA聚合酶柔性α-CTD结构域加速蛋白-DNA结合的通用物理机制，虽非典型TF-DNA体系，但蛋白-DNA结合动力学建模方法对TF-DNA互作研究有重要借鉴价值。
abstract: Bacterial RNA polymerases (RNAPs) have two flexibly tethered α subunit C-terminal domains (α-CTDs) that bind DNA. Interaction between α-CTDs and some promoter DNA motifs is known to accelerate transcription initiation, but the physical mechanism by which it does so is unclear. We used single-molecule multiwavelength fluorescence microscopy to test how the diffusion-limited binding kinetics of core RNAP to non-promoter DNA differ from those of mutant RNAPs that lack one or both α-CTDs. We find that even though α-CTDs and their tethers are small compared to the complete RNAP molecule, the presence of two α-CTDs accelerates DNA binding by ∼10-fold and ∼55-fold respectively relative to RNAP constructs in which one or both α-CTDs are deleted. In contrast, the presence of α-CTDs did not have a detectable effect on RNAP-DNA complex lifetimes in the absence of RNA synthesis. We explain how α-CTDs achieve the dramatic acceleration of RNAP binding to DNA using a quantitative three-state kinetic model that includes a transient binding intermediate where only the α-CTD(s) are bound to DNA, tethering the rest of the RNAP in the vicinity of DNA. The model and assumed parameters are validated using Brownian dynamics simulations of the DNA association reactions for two-, one-, or zero-CTD RNAP constructs. The combination of single-molecule experiments, mathematical theory, and simulations suggests that adding a flexible DNA-binding tether is a general physical mechanism which can accelerate the diffusion-limited binding of a large protein like RNAP to DNA and quantitatively defines the conditions under which this acceleration can occur. Significance Statement Large enzymes that must associate with DNA to perform their biological functions are expected to bind DNA only slowly because of slow enzyme diffusion. However, some DNA-binding enzymes have one or more additional small DNA-binding domains that can diffuse rapidly but are attached to the enzyme through an unstructured flexible tether. Combining single-molecule experiments, theory, and computation, we present evidence for a general mechanism by which such tethered domains can accelerate enzyme binding to DNA by orders of magnitude, while not significantly changing the duration of the DNA-bound state. We demonstrate this effect for the flexibly-tethered α-subunit C-terminal domain of bacterial RNA polymerase. The mechanism may allow the polymerase to rapidly bind DNA while minimizing non-functional sequestration on the genome.
abstract_zh:
细菌RNA聚合酶（RNAPs）具有两个柔性连接的α亚基C端结构域（α-CTDs），这些结构域能够结合DNA。已知α-CTDs与某些启动子DNA基序之间的相互作用能加速转录起始，但其物理机制尚不清楚。我们利用单分子多波长荧光显微镜，测试了核心RNA聚合酶与非启动子DNA的扩散限制结合动力学，与缺失一个或两个α-CTDs的突变RNA聚合酶相比有何差异。我们发现，尽管α-CTDs及其连接链相对于完整的RNAP分子较小，但两个α-CTDs的存在使DNA结合速度分别比缺失一个或两个α-CTDs的RNAP构建体加快约10倍和约55倍。相反，在无RNA合成的情况下，α-CTDs的存在对RNAP-DNA复合物的寿命没有可检测的影响。我们通过一个定量三态动力学模型解释了α-CTDs如何实现RNAP与DNA结合的显著加速，该模型包括一个瞬态结合中间体，其中仅α-CTD(s)与DNA结合，将RNAP的其余部分系留在DNA附近。该模型及假设参数通过布朗动力学模拟验证，模拟了二、一或零CTD RNAP构建体的DNA结合反应。单分子实验、数学理论和模拟的结合表明，添加柔性DNA结合系链是一种通用物理机制，可加速像RNAP这样的大蛋白与DNA的扩散限制结合，并定量定义了这种加速发生的条件。  
**意义声明**：必须与DNA结合以执行其生物功能的大型酶，由于酶扩散缓慢，预期其与DNA的结合速度较慢。然而，一些DNA结合酶具有一个或多个额外的小型DNA结合结构域，这些结构域可以快速扩散，但通过非结构化的柔性系链附着在酶上。结合单分子实验、理论和计算，我们提出证据支持一种通用机制，即此类系链结构域可以将酶与DNA的结合加速数个数量级，同时不显著改变DNA结合状态的持续时间。我们以细菌RNA聚合酶的柔性系链α亚基C端结构域为例展示了这一效应。该机制可能使聚合酶快速结合DNA，同时最小化基因组上的非功能性隔离。
